The petitioner argued that he filed the application within six months from the rejection of his second appeal on 16.4.1987 by the Director General and as such it was not time barred as alleged. 

 2. The Administrative Tribunal took the view that when the proviso to section 4(2) requires the decision of a higher administrative authority to be obtained before filing a case before the Tribunal, it should not be disqualification if a person before coming to the Tribunal moves next higher authority and gets a decision (after rejection of a first appeal) and accordingly decided the point of limitation in favour of the petitioner. The application was also allowed on merit. On appeal, however, the Administrative Appellate Tribunal set aside the order of the Administrative Tribunal taking the view that the application before the Tribunal having been filed after a period of about two years from the date of rejection of the first appeal on 8.8.1985 the same was hopelessly barred by limitation. 

 3. Seeking leave to appeal from the impugned judgment of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Mr. Md. Korban Ali, learned Advocate for the petitioner, sup-ported the view taken by the Tribunal and argued that the second appeal was filed by the petitioner in good faith to the Director General of Food as the highest authority and as such it could not be said that the application for petition was barred by limitation. 

 4. The view taken by the. Administrative Tribunal was apparently wrong in that the second proviso to section 4(2) of the Act prescribes the period of limitation of six months inter alia, from the date of "making of the decision on the matter by the higher administrative authority". It does not say that the aggrieved person must go to the highest authority seeking redress of his grievance. He has to seek remedy as provided under the law. The Appellate Tribunal found that under rule 17 of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 an appeal is provided against the order passed under the said Rules which the petitioner had availed of and was rejected by the Director (Administration) on 8.8.1985. There is no second appeal under the said Rules and as such the petitioner had no further remedy under the law after 

 rejection of his appeal. Mr. Korban Ali could not show any provision of law that a second appeal lay. The petitioner might have gone to the Director General with a second appeal bonafide for relief but the said appeal not being provided by any law, the limitation for the purpose of section 4 of the Act would run from the date of the rejection of the first appeal. The view taken by the Appellate Tribunal was, therefore, right.
